speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The gate looked at every face coming north, and it looked at mine. They heard every word of the old man, and that was worse. Tell me the flag, and then tell me the book.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The flag went up after two dark days and took under three hundred. That is the count from the door, and I will stand by Margery's stair before I stand by a guess.

speaker: margery_pell
text: Old men, and country folk who'd not heard. Nine shillings in mine, and I never took it so quiet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then quiet is the news. I am glad of nine shillings that are yours. I did not come to claim them.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Errors, at two, the bill they struck yesterday. You gave them the whole tale and they sat still for it. A thin house is a quiet one.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Too quiet. A tale wants a cough or two in it. The book is the errand now.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Noon yesterday. I have had them since then. A shirt. Abel, they are yours to rule. I am done holding them.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thou hast held them long enough, Dick. Give them.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: I am not your cousin, and these want ruling.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Rule them. They were read aloud once, at a table, and that is the only order they have had.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Six days. I will not be hurried because the city is loud. A fair book that is not fair is a quarrel with the Master before he has the string off it.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Six days. My man carries the fair book to Clerkenwell on Monday. Not before Monday, and not by you, Will. You are not a carrier this week.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Seven shillings, set by for the fee. Not paid. Paid when the book is in his hand.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Set by, and not entered as spent. I will keep it apart from the day's takings. Margery's nine is not this seven.

speaker: margery_pell
text: Nine is mine, in the box at the stair, and I did not take it with any shouting. I can bear one quiet day. Do not give me a summer of them and call it peace.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: The watch at the gate looked at the shirt as if a shirt might be a speech. They did not open it. Thou mayst walk home by the same road, Will. It is dull, and dull is the virtue left to us.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Same road. I am not going back for a line I think of in the night.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: If you think of a better word, write it small, and expect no thanks. I am ruling a king, not keeping a correspondence.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No better word tonight. The king Dick gave you is the king we read. Send that one.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Home. Monday is the carry. Monday is not tonight, and it is not a decision about the roads either. The roads can keep.

speaker: margery_pell
text: I am shutting the stair. Old men are a poor harvest and an easy one. I have said the nine shillings. I will not say them twice for the pleasure of hearing myself.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: My arm is empty. I find I can bear an empty arm better than a crown in a frightened week.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Bear it. We are not playing him.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Bear it on the road. I am locking a thin day in, and I do not want the epilogue on the step.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Go. Six days, and a lodging at the end of your road. I have the leaves. You have had your scene.
